transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. I'm a clinic manager, and things are generally really good, but... I guess what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I've been having these little moments at work. 

Like, I'll start an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in a metrics meeting with every intention of really tracking everything. But then, within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far that... well, I just sort of wander off mentally. I'll catch myself rereading the same numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the whole point of the discussion. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really should be on top of these things at my age. It's probably just normal stress, right? But... does that make sense? Am I explaining that okay?
About how long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your focus and concentration?

Well, I mean, it's not like I've been completely unable to do my job or anything. I've always been pretty organized, honestly. But... I guess I'd say I really started noticing it more since my last promotion. That was about two years and four months ago. 

I took on a larger portfolio, and... I don't know, maybe I just haven't adapted as well as I should have? The little systems I used to rely on to keep track of everything just started feeling really overwhelming with the extra workload. I'm sure anyone would struggle a bit with a step up like that, don't you think? I just hope I'm not wasting your time with something that's just a normal adjustment period.
Over these past couple of years, how has your overall mood been—have you felt persistently down, low, or depressed?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed. I mean, I have my days where I feel a little frustrated with myself, especially when I drop the ball on a report or space out during a meeting, but... I think that's pretty normal, right? 

Overall, my mood is actually quite good. I have a lot to be thankful for—a great job, good colleagues. I'm generally a pretty positive person. I just get a little down on myself sometimes when I can't seem to focus like I know I should be able to. But definitely nothing like being persistently low or depressed. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Well, um... I guess if I really think back... I mean, I was a good kid, I promise! I never got into trouble or anything like that. But, um... I suppose there were some little things. 

Like, I remember in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright, but... maybe a little careless sometimes? I think they just meant I rushed through things because I was eager, you know? And, well, my mom did usually sit with me while I did my homework. Not because I couldn't do it, but just... I had a habit of maybe losing track of what the actual assignment was, or I'd accidentally leave my math book in my desk at school. 

It wasn't a huge problem, just normal kid stuff, I think. I mean, a lot of kids forget their books sometimes, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student... is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
Outside of work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about various everyday things, to the point where it feels hard to control?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I worry excessively. I mean, I care about things, obviously. I want to make sure the bills are paid on time and that my family is doing well, but I think that's just being responsible, isn't it? 

I definitely don't feel like my worrying is out of control or anything like that. I'm usually pretty good at keeping things in perspective outside of the office. I just... I like to make sure everything is taken care of. That's a good thing, right? I'm not the kind of person who just sits around agonizing over every little thing.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 (generalized anxiety disorder) as the patient denies excessive, uncontrollable worry outside of work.
